scripts/deploy_nonprod_vm.sh: Per call unique remote outcome path /tmp/pantheon-refresh-outcome-<run>-<epoch>-<pid>-<random>.json and PANTHEON_REFRESH_CALL_ID / PANTHEON_REFRESH_RUN_ID exported to the remote script
Every outcome writer stamps call_id; the runner (verify_refresh_outcome_belongs_to_call) replaces an outcome without its own call id by a failed record whose reason starts outcome_call_mismatch

steady check: steady_check_settle_refresh_orphans finds refresh-only processes of the same run via /proc/<pid>/environ, waits STEADY_CHECK_ORPHAN_WAIT_SECONDS (default 180) then SIGTERM (its own handler restores services, up to 60s) then SIGKILL, records orphan {action ended|stopped, pids, seconds}

steady check: waits at most start period + one interval (read from docker inspect, 120s fallback, once per container) while health is starting; still starting at the bound fails with reason <service>_starting; a healthy service is judged at once
steady check: removes /tmp/pantheon-refresh-outcome-<run>-* and dot-prefixed temp variants of its run except its own output, records cleanup {files, bytes}
changes.unchanged: deploy components other than refresh-only; scripts/run_with_dev_environment_lease.sh; scripts/dev_remote_guarded_exec.py; the workflow file needed no change

leftover_files.most_that_can_remain_if_steady_check_doe: one file per refresh-only call of the run (each is removed by its own runner after copy-back unless the runner is killed first). Each file is one JSON object with a redacted log tail of at most 200 lines, so tens of KB. The next steady check of the same run id would remove them; files of a run whose steady check never ran stay in /tmp until reboot or manual removal
leftover_files.lock_files: scripts/deploy_nonprod_vm.sh creates no lock file for refresh calls; the environment lease lock belongs to run_with_dev_environment_lease.sh which is out of scope

residual_findings: The FinMind fundamentals step 15 minute timeout belongs to the market-data owner.
